name: agent-fs-write-operations
body:
Code-writer implementer agents must be able to delete, move, and copy files inside the surface they own, so a plan task with a `deletes` / `renames` / `moves` verb is implementable. (Historic motivation: the generated implementers carried only shallow bash `rm <dir>/*.<ext>` grants and no `mv`/`cp`.)

The capability is delivered by a small suite of filesystem tools — `apg_rm`, `apg_mv`, `apg_cp` — installed by `apg init`, which SELF-ENFORCE their scope: each tool reads the acting agent's own granted path globs (from the caller's agent permission block, via the opencode plugin context) and refuses any path not matched by them, with the grants and the candidate resolved in one consistent frame. The tool-level grant (deny-by-default) is only the callability gate; per-path scoping lives inside the tool. For a code-writer the granted globs are WORKTREE-ONLY — `apg/.worktrees/*/<glob>`, never the repo-root path (amended by `requirements.requirement.code-writer-worktree-only-writes`): opencode resolves path-scoped globs against the session workspace root (the main checkout), so the worktree form is what reaches the worktree, and a root grant would make main writable. This is a scoped capability, never a blanket grant: a path outside the agent's granted globs is refused, a path resolving into the main checkout is refused, and an operation may not cross the project/worktree boundary. The suite tools replace the shallow bash `rm <dir>/*.<ext>` grants.

Scope: rm + mv + cp only. Product source (`opencode-suite/**` tool files, `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts`, `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`) plus the binary's install registry (`rust.apg.install`'s `SUITE_TOOLS`). NOT the repo's own `.opencode/agents/**`. Plain filesystem operations only — no `git rm`/`git mv` — and no change to the binary's node/edge mutation surface.

Acceptance criteria:
- `apg init` installs the three tools into `~/.opencode/tools/`: `rust.apg.install`'s `SUITE_TOOLS` carries one entry per new tool.
- A generated implementer agent is granted `apg_rm`/`apg_mv`/`apg_cp` scoped to exactly its owned path globs under `apg/.worktrees/*/` (worktree-only; no repo-root variant), replacing the shallow bash `rm` grants; the tool self-enforces that scope per path.
- An fs-op whose source path (and, for mv/cp, destination path) is matched by the agent's granted globs succeeds; a path outside them is refused.
- An fs-op whose path escapes the project/worktree boundary, or resolves into the main checkout, is refused.
- The install-assertion e2e (`rust.main_e2e.e2e.suite_installs_node_edge_project_tools_and_retires_spec_invariant`) asserts the three tools are embedded and installed, and stays green.
